newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Nov 28.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Detectives told on Wednesday of their "nightmares of nightmares" of having to investigate covertly a fellow police officer who had won huge sympathy from police and public for his escape from a satanic assailant. Brent Garner, 32, a Palmerston North fraud squad detective, on Wednesday admitted in Palmerston North District Court to faking his torture and attempted murder and to the arson of his Ashurst house on October 18. He will be sentenced on December 13. Page 1.

The Alliance has promised to keep its lips sealed over negotiations between Labour and NZ First, in return for seeing any coalition agreement before it is made public. Speaking after a two-hour meeting between the two parties on Wednesday night, leader Jim Anderton said the Alliance had undertaken to respect confidentiality between Labour and NZ First. In return, Anderton said Labour had assured the Alliance it would be given time to consider and comment on the details of any agreement between Labour and NZ First. Page 1.

ACT NZ deputy leader Ken Shirley said on Wednesday it was most unlikely his party would enter a National-NZ First coalition. But he indicated ACT would support it on crucial votes in Parliament. Page 2.

NZ First MPs expect to choose between coalition offers pre-approved by the Labour and National caucuses, despite some National MPs' misgivings. MPs in National, Labour and NZ First said on Wednesday they were still unsure how the last stages of coalition-forming would happen. National MP Joy McLauchlan said she could not see how National could commit itself to a deal before NZ First did. A coalition would have to be formed under a "bilateral agreement" in which the parties sat down and signed together, she said. Page 2.
Queenstown people who do not want a casino in their town may launch a petition calling for a referendum banning more casinos in New Zealand. Page 2.

The two-year-long economic slowdown should hit bottom in the March and June quarters of 1997 and interest rates should ease in the coming six months, according to Westpac Bank. Though the economy is expected to slow down to about 1.8 percent growth by the middle of next year, the medium-term outlook is brighter, Westpac says.
Page 15.

The New Zealand Government should take retaliatory action against Australia for its insistence on blocking New Zealand salmon imports, listed fishing company Sanford says. Sanford managing director David Anderson says in the company's annual report that there is a blatant trade barrier to New Zealand salmon exports to Australia. Page 15.

A rebound in export growth was projected in the December economic and fiscal update, Deputy Finance Minister Lockwood Smith said on Wednesday. The update is due to be made public on Monday by Finance Minister Bill Birch. Page 15.

Westpac Banking Corp has revived its Asian strategy in an alliance with British bank Standard and Chartered which will allow it to provide select banking services for clients operating in Asia. The deal will target management services, local Asian currency lending, local transaction facilities and trade finance facilities, and will be available to New Zealand clients of Westpac. Page 15.

Air New Zealand was on the verge of making the first of what was likely to be a series of announcements on global alliances, chairman Bob Matthew said on Wednesday. "We are optimistic of putting in place significant alliance initiatives and the market won't have to wait too long for them," he said. "The work is largely done." Speculation has been mounting that Air NZ and Ansett Australia, in which it recently acquired a half share, will make alliances with big airlines in North America, Asia and Europe. Page 16.

Brierley Investments was comfortable with its 6.8 percent stake in Coles Myer and had no intention of seeking control of the giant Australian retailer, BIL chairman Bob Matthew said on Wednesday. Page 16.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Labour's bargaining position in the coalition talks was bolstered on Wednesday night by a two-hour meeting with the Alliance which saw long-standing differences put to one side to help Labour to strike a deal with NZ First. Top of the agenda was how to define confidence issues and reach an understanding that avoids the Alliance being trapped into having to support the coalition on matters it considers undeserving or frivolous. Labour leader Helen Clark and her Alliance counterpart Jim Anderton emerged positive and relaxed from the meeting in contrast to last week's sniping.

Grey Power is warning of dangers in NZ First's compulsory superannuation scheme. In a letter to all MPs that arrived at Parliament on Wednesday in time for pending caucus talks on coalition proposals, it endorses the type of scheme advocated
by Labour.

Employers are being urged to take great care when sacking sick staff, after a worker who was away for more than six months with dermatitis won an unfair dismissal case. The Northern Employers and Manufacturers' Association is reminding members that they cannot just claim frustration of contract.

The economy has the potential to rocket away once interest and exchange rates fall, according to the Owens Group managing director Rodger Fisher. He was commenting as the Auckland-based transport company, after a flat trading period, reported a 4.2 percent higher tax-paid profit of $4.93 million for the September half-year. Fisher said the group was trading solidly in New Zealand, while in Australia greater emphasis was placed on margins, rather than sales.

The erratic trading which characterised The Warehouse Group's first quarter had continued this month, the retailer's managing director Stephen Tindall told the annual meeting on Wednesday. Bad weather and political uncertainty were possible reasons for the indifferent sales this month.
The New Zealand dollar trade-weighted exchange rate index finished at its lowest level in almost six weeks on Wednesday as financial markets quietly awaited the outcome of coalition talks.
